skill.name: convex
skill.description: Find the right Convex guide for starting an app, writing TypeScript backend code, adding components, or maintaining a deployment.
skill.summary: Route Convex development and operations tasks to specialist skills.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: Eleven static matches are false positives: Markdown formatting or a documentation link. The capability route explicitly fetches a remote catalog, and the setup guidance recommends an unpinned CLI invocation. Separate findings cover trust in remote procedures and a transcript-sharing workflow whose consent and redaction safeguards are not stated here.

remediation.issue: Mutable remote procedures are preferred over bundled guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Pin remote procedures to a reviewed version or verify a signed manifest. Require explicit approval before remote guidance can trigger installs, data transfers, or deployment changes.

remediation.issue: The setup recommendation does not pin the Convex CLI version.
remediation.suggestion: Use the project's verified, locked Convex CLI version or specify an exact trusted version. Ask before running the installer and show the files it will change.

remediation.issue: The transcript feedback listing does not state consent, preview, or redaction requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit opt-in before sharing. Show the recipient and a redacted preview, and send only the excerpts needed for feedback.

content.value_statement: Starting or maintaining a Convex app can require several specialized guides. This skill routes your task to the relevant companion skill or capability catalog entry.
actual_capabilities: Directs new full-stack projects to Convex Quickstart.
Routes schema, query, mutation, and action work to Convex Expert.
Points feature requests such as authentication, search, and scheduling to Convex Add and its online catalog.
Distinguishes backend correctness review, authorization audit, and behavior verification.
Routes live operations to separate guides for monitoring, migration rehearsal, cost analysis, and bundle size.
limitations: This file routes tasks but does not contain the full companion procedures.
The online capability catalog requires network access and can change after this skill is installed.
Some setup and operations require separate tools, project access, or deployment permissions.
The router cannot guarantee correctness, security, or production readiness.

use_cases.title: Start a full-stack prototype
use_cases.description: Identify the Quickstart route for a new Convex application and set a narrow first milestone.

use_cases.title: Add a feature to an existing app
use_cases.description: Find the companion guide for a recurring job, authentication setup, or search feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare a live-data migration
use_cases.description: Identify the preview rehearsal route and separate validation from any production change.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starting guide
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a shared task list from scratch. Which Convex skill should I use first, and what should the first milestone be? Do not install anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a recurring job
prompt_templates.prompt: My Convex app needs a nightly cleanup job. Identify the relevant guide and list what I should verify before adding it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an authorization review
prompt_templates.prompt: Which Convex skills should review and verify access to project records? Outline checks for ownership and unauthorized reads without changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Rehearse a live migration
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to backfill a field in a live Convex app. Choose the rehearsal route and outline preview checks, rollback criteria, and the production approval step.

output_examples.input: Which guide should I use to start a shared task list?
output_examples.output: Start with Convex Quickstart. For the first milestone, store one task and confirm that an update appears in a second browser session.

output_examples.input: Which guides can help me verify that users see only their own records?
output: Use Convex Authz to review identity and ownership checks in public queries and mutations.
Use Convex Verify to plan tests for an owner, another signed-in user, and an unauthenticated caller.

output_examples.input: Where should I start before backfilling a field on live data?
output_examples.output: Use Convex Migrate Rehearse on a preview deployment. Verify the backfill and define rollback criteria before requesting approval for production.

best_practices: Identify whether you are starting a project, adding a feature, or operating a live deployment.
Review online procedures before acting, and use bundled guidance when the catalog is unavailable.
Name the target deployment and obtain approval before production changes or paid operations.
anti_patterns: Treating this routing file as a substitute for the specialist procedure.
Running an installer or making a deployment change based only on unreviewed remote instructions.
Sharing a full session transcript without reviewing its contents, confirming the recipient, and obtaining consent.

faq.question: Which guide should I use for a new Convex app?
faq.answer: Use Convex Quickstart for a new full-stack project.

faq.question: Where should I start when editing Convex functions?
faq.answer: Start with Convex Expert for schemas, validators, indexes, and backend function patterns.

faq.question: How do I find guidance for adding a feature?
faq.answer: Use Convex Add to find a matching procedure in the online capability catalog.

faq.question: What happens when the catalog is unavailable?
faq.answer: Use the bundled companion procedure when one is available.

faq.question: Which guides cover authorization?
faq.answer: Use Convex Authz to review access controls and Convex Verify to plan tests for permitted and denied actions.

faq.question: Does this skill authorize paid operations or production changes?
faq.answer: No. Confirm paid operations explicitly and obtain separate approval before acting on a production deployment.
